source_text: Οἱ δὲ παραδιδόντες τὰ μυθοποιηθέντα ὑπὸ τῶν ποιητῶν οὐδεμίαν ἀπόδειξιν φέρουσι τοῖς ἐκμανθάνουσι νέοις, καὶ ἐπὶ ἀπάτῃ καὶ ἀπαγωγῇ τοῖ ἀνθρωπείου γένους εἰρῆσθαι ἀποδείκνυμεν κατ᾿ ἐνέργειαν τῶν φαύλων δαιμόνων. Ἀκούσαντες γὰρ διὰ τῶν προφητῶν κηρυσσόμενον παραγενησόμενον τὸν Χριστόν, καὶ κολασθησομένους διὰ πυρὸς τοὺς ἀσεβεῖς τῶν ἀνθρώπων, προεβάλλοντο πολλοὺς λεχθῆναι γενομένους υἱοὺς τῷ Διῒ, νομίζοντες δυνήσεσθαι ἐνεργῆσαι τερατολογίαν ἡγήσασθαι τοὺς ἀνθρώπους τὰ περὶ τὸν Χριστὸν καὶ ὅμοια τοῖς ὑπὸ τῶν ποιητῶν λεχθεῖσι. Καὶ ταῦτα δ᾿ ἐλέχθη καὶ ἐν Ἕλλησι καὶ ἐν ἔθνεσι πᾶσιν, ὅπου μᾶλλον ἐπήκουον τῶν προφητῶν πιστευθήσεσθαι τὸν Χριστὸν προκηρυσσόντων. Ὅτι δὲ καὶ ἀκούοντες τὰ διὰ τῶν προφητῶν λεγόμενα οὐκ ἐνόουν ἀκριβῶς, ἀλλ᾿ ὡς πλανώμενοι ἐμιμήσαντο τὼ περὶ τὸν ἡμέτερον Χριστόν, διασαφήσομεν. Μωϋσῆς οὖν ὁ προφῄτης, ὡς προέφημεν, πρεσβύτερος ἦν πόντων συγγραφέων, καὶ δι᾿ αὐτοῦ, ὡς προεμηνύσαμεν, προεφητεύθη οὕτως· Οὐκ ἐκλείψει ἄρχων ἐξ Ἰούδα καὶ ἡγούμενος ἐκ τῶν μηρῶν αὐτοῦ, ἕως ἂν ἔλθῃ ᾧ ἀπόκειται· καὶ αὐτὸς ἔσται προσδοκία ἐθνῶν, δεσμεύων πρὸς ἄμπελον τὸν πῶλον αἰτοῦ, πλύνων τὴν στολὴν αὐτοῦ ἐν αἵματι σταφυλῆς“. Τούτων οὖν τᾶν προφητικῶν λόγων ἀκούσαντες οἱ δαίμονες Διόνυσον μὲν ἔφασαν γεγονέναι υἱὸν τοῦ Διός, εὑρετὴν δὲ γενέσθαι ἀμπέλου παρέδωκαν, καὶ ὄνον ἐν τοῖς μυστηρίοις αἰτοῦ ἀναγράφουσι, καὶ διασπαραχθέντα αὐτὸν ἀνεληλυθέναι εἰς οὐρανὸν ἐδίδαξαν. Καὶ ἐπειδὴ διὰ τῆς Μωϋσέως προφητείας οὐ ῥητῶς ἐσημαίνετο, εἴτε υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ ὁ παραγενησόμενός ἐστι, καὶ εἰ ὀχούμενος ἐπὶ πώλου ἐπὶ γῆς μενεῖ ἢ εἰς οὐρανὸν ἀνελεύσεται, καὶ τὸ τοῦ πώλου ὄνομα καὶ ὄνου πᾶλον καὶ ἵππου σημαίνειν ἐδύνατο, μὴ ἐπιστάμενοι εἴτε ὄνου πῶλον ἄγων ἔσται σύμβολον τῆς παρουσίας αἰτοῖ εἴτε ἵππου ὁ προκηρυσσόμενος, καὶ υἱὸς θεοῖ ἐστιν, ὡς προέφημεν, ἢ ἀνθρώπου, τὸν Βελλεροφόντην καὶ αὐτὸν ἐφ᾿ ἵππου Πηγασου, ἄνθρωπον ἐξ ἀνθρώπων γενόμενον, εἰς οὐρανὸν ἔφασαν ἀνεληλυθέναι. Ὅτι δὲ ἤκουσαν διὰ τοῦ ἄλλου προφήτου Ἡσαΐου λεχθέν, ὅτι διὰ παρθένου τεχθήσεται καὶ δι᾿ ἑαυτοῦ ἀνελεύσεται εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν, τὸν Περσέα λεχθῆναι προεβάλλοντο. Καὶ ὅτε ἔγνωσαν εἰρημένον, ὡς προλέλεκται ἐν ταῖς προγεγραμμέναις προφητείαις, Ἰσχυρὸς ἁ ς γίγας δραμεῖν ὁδόν“, τὸν Ἡρακλέα ἰσχυρὸν καὶ ἐκπερινοστήσαντα τὴν πᾶσαν γῆν ἔφασαν. Ὅτε δὲ πάλιν ἐμαθον προφητευθέντα θεραπεύσειν αὐτὸν πᾶσαν νόσον καὶ νεκροὺς ἀνεγερεῖν, τὶν Ἀσκληπιὸν παρήνεγκαν.
pass_a_gloss: Those who hand down the things that have been mythologized by the poets bring no proof to the young people who learn them, and we demonstrate that they are spoken by the agency of evil demons to deceive and lead astray the human race. For when the demons heard through the prophets that Christ was going to come, and that the impious among men would be punished by fire, they put forward that many had been born as sons of Zeus, thinking that they would be able to effect a deception so that people would think that the things about Christ and similar things spoken by the poets had already occurred. And these things were said both among the Greeks and among all the nations where the prophets were more likely to be believed as they proclaimed Christ in advance. That those who heard the things spoken through the prophets did not understand them accurately, but imitated the things about our Christ as if they were wandering, we will make clear. Moses the prophet, as we said before, was older than the writers of histories, and through him, as we previously indicated, it was prophesied in this way: A ruler will not fail from Judah, and a leader from his loins, until he comes to whom it has been reserved; and he will be the expectation of the nations, binding his donkey to a vine, washing his robe in the blood of grapes. When the demons heard these prophetic words, they said that Dionysus was the son of Zeus, and they handed down that he was the discoverer of the vine, and they wrote that a donkey was present in the mysteries of the goat, and they taught that he had been torn apart and had gone up into heaven. And since it was not clearly indicated through Moses' prophecy whether the one who was going to come was the son of God, and whether he would be carried on a donkey on the earth or would go up into heaven, and the name of the donkey and the foal could also mean horse, not knowing whether the one who was going to be proclaimed would be led by a donkey as a symbol of his presence or by a horse, and whether he was the son of God or of a man, they said that Bellerophon, who was a man born of men, had gone up into heaven on the horse Pegasus. That they heard through another prophet, Isaiah, that he would be born of a virgin and would go up into heaven by himself, they put forward that Perseus was spoken of. And when they learned that it had been said, as previously spoken in the aforementioned prophecies, The strong giant will run the road, they said that Hercules, who was strong and had traveled around the whole earth, was spoken of. And when they learned again that he had been prophesied to heal every disease and raise the dead, they brought forward Asclepius.

bible_refs.note: Moses' prophecy about the coming ruler

pass_b_english: Those who hand down the stories mythologized by the poets offer no proof to the young people who learn them, and we demonstrate that these tales are spoken through the agency of evil demons to deceive and lead astray the human race. For when the demons heard through the prophets that Christ was going to come, and that the impious among humanity would be punished by fire, they put forward the claim that many had been born as sons of Zeus, thinking they could effect a deception so that people would regard the things about Christ — and similar things spoken by the poets — as events that had already occurred. These fabrications were circulated both among the Greeks and among all the nations where the prophets were more likely to be believed as they proclaimed Christ in advance. We will make clear that those who heard the words spoken through the prophets did not understand them accurately, but imitated the things concerning our Christ as if they were wandering in error. Moses the prophet, as we said before, was older than all writers of histories, and through him, as we previously indicated, it was prophesied in this way: 'A ruler will not fail from Judah, and a leader from his loins, until he comes to whom it has been reserved; and he will be the expectation of the nations, binding his donkey to a vine, washing his robe in the blood of grapes' (Genesis 49:10-11). When the demons heard these prophetic words, they declared that Dionysus was the son of Zeus, handed down that he was the discoverer of the vine, wrote that a donkey was present in the mysteries of the goat, and taught that he had been torn apart and had ascended into heaven. Since Moses' prophecy did not clearly indicate whether the coming one was the Son of God, whether he would remain on earth riding a donkey or ascend into heaven, and since the term for 'donkey' could also mean foal or horse, the demons did not know whether the proclaimed one would be led by a donkey as a symbol of his presence or by a horse, or whether he was the Son of God or of a man, as we said before; therefore they said that Bellerophon, a man born of men, had ascended into heaven on the horse Pegasus. When they heard through the other prophet Isaiah that he would be born of a virgin and would ascend into heaven by himself, they put forward that Perseus was the one spoken of. And when they learned that it had been said, as previously spoken in the aforementioned prophecies, 'The strong giant will run the road,' they declared that Hercules, who was strong and had traveled around the whole earth, was the one meant. When they learned again that he had been prophesied to heal every disease and raise the dead, they brought forward Asclepius.
